answer_text:
Let

\[
\alpha=\sqrt[80]{43}, \qquad \beta=\sqrt[84]{43}.
\]

We want

\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta):\mathbb{Q}].
\]

First compute the least common multiple of \(80\) and \(84\):

\[
80=2^4\cdot 5,\qquad 84=2^2\cdot 3\cdot 7,
\]

so

\[
\operatorname{lcm}(80,84)=2^4\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdot 7=1680.
\]

Let

\[
\gamma=\sqrt[1680]{43}.
\]

Then

\[
\alpha=43^{1/80}=\gamma^{21}, \qquad \beta=43^{1/84}=\gamma^{20}.
\]

Now observe that

\[
\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=\frac{\gamma^{21}}{\gamma^{20}}=\gamma.
\]

Thus \(\gamma\in \mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta)\). Conversely, since \(\alpha=\gamma^{21}\) and \(\beta=\gamma^{20}\), we have

\[
\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta)\subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\gamma).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta)=\mathbb{Q}(\gamma).
\]

So the desired degree is

\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\gamma):\mathbb{Q}].
\]

The element \(\gamma\) satisfies

\[
x^{1680}-43=0.
\]

The polynomial \(x^{1680}-43\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb{Q}\) by Eisenstein’s criterion at the prime \(43\): every non-leading coefficient is divisible by \(43\), and the constant term \(-43\) is not divisible by \(43^2\).

Hence the minimal polynomial of \(\gamma\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\) has degree \(1680\), so

\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta):\mathbb{Q}]=1680.
\]

\[
\boxed{1680}
\]
